Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

familiar adjective

well known, recognised

also well known, known, it looks familiar, that sounds familiar, unfamiliar

classical

Cic. Mil. 76: quae nōta sunt omnibus (Lewis & Short, s.v. nōscō)
Cic. Sull. 72: vīta P. Sullae vōbīs populōque Rōmānō nōtissima

nōtus, nōta, nōtum

adjective; the person to whom it is known in the dative

known, familiar

The plain word: mihi nōtus est, “I know him, he’s familiar to me”. Ignōtus is unfamiliar.

Other words

  • familiāris, familiāre — of the household; intimate; familiar

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Petr. 100: vōx auribus meīs familiāris (Lewis & Short); Quint. 5.10.96: familiāribus magis eī aetātī exemplīs

    First “of the household” (rēs familiāris, one’s property), then “intimate, friendly”, and as a noun a close friend (Cic. Lael. 39). The sense “well known, familiar” to the ears or the mind is post-Augustan (Petronius, Quintilian); in Cicero’s Latin say nōtus.

Examples

  • fingī haec putātis, quae patent, quae nōta sunt omnibus, quae tenentur?

    do you think these things are invented, which are plain, which everyone knows, which are proved?Cic. Mil. 76 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōta mihi est haec vōx.

    I know that voice.composed

See also familiar, know.

SourcesLewis & Short: nosco · Lewis & Short: familiaris

Cicero, Petronius and Quintilian quoted as Lewis & Short quotes them.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
